name: colon-any
description: The `: any` type ANNOTATION is the uncounted sibling of the ratcheted `as any` cast (audit F-06-1). `: any` on a tenant key (organizationId), a money value, an auth field, or external input erases the type checker exactly as `as any` does — the leads.organizationId-widening class the as-any ratchet exists to stop, walking straight past it because that ratchet only matches the `as any` cast form. This freezes the annotation count over server/ and drives it DOWN. Remediate the tenant-key/money/auth subset first; lower baselineCount as annotations are typed away. New `: any` now fails CI.
lastBumpNote: 2940 -> 2936 on 2026-08-19: deletion-revealed, not a refactor. `atlasContextInjector.ts`, `communicationDeduplication.ts` and `userAiCostControls.ts` were deleted (deletion ledger 2026-08-19) after lint-reachability was taught to strip comments and showed all three were module orphans — each had been reading as imported because its own docblock opened with a usage example the scanner took for real code. Two of the three carried the same lazy-Redis shape (`let _redis: any`, `Promise<any | null>`, `const IORedis = (await import("ioredis")).default`), which is where these counts came from. Locked in per the strictly-down rule: the reduction belongs to the commit that earned it. PRIOR NOTE — 2942 -> 2941 on 2026-08-18: FOUNDER KILL RULING — the shadowed second `/api/config/features` handler in routes-admin.ts. The annotation was its `catch (err: any)`. The handler was unreachable (routes.ts:405 registers first and wins) and returned a stale shape: enabledKeys/enabledRoutes only, no deny-lists and none of the controlled* fields the client needs to tell an ungoverned route from a disabled one. A deletion, not a typing improvement. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. PRIOR NOTE — 2950 -> 2942 on 2026-08-18: FOUNDRY TRANSFER — OUTCOME OBSERVATION. A typing improvement this time, not a deletion. server/services/outcomeVerificationLoop.ts's four verifiers took `(action: any, payload: any, orgId: number)` and returned `agentCodename: action.agentCodename` — a column `agent_events` DOES NOT HAVE, which the file's own comment says at the top of the loop ('agent_events has no agentCodename column; it is carried in the payload') before reading the payload correctly. `action: any` is exactly why nobody noticed the contradiction: every genuinely OBSERVED verification reached trust evolution attributed to `undefined`, while the self-reported ones kept their name. Replaced by one `ActionUnderReview` interface carrying the resolved codename, org and timestamp, which typed away eight annotations. This is the annotation form of the class the ratchet was written for: not a widened tenant key, but an untyped row standing in for a schema that disagreed with it. Locked in per this ratchet's strictly-down rule. minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 1370 file(s) (server/**/*.ts minus tests). Floor set to 1100, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
